 Chief Metropolitan Magistrate on the accusations, inter alia, that she was married to accused petitioner No. 1 on 18.6.97. At the time of marriage her father made a gift worth about Tk. 4 Lacs in cash and in kind. After marriage they were living peacefully. But sometime thereafter petitioner No. 1 and his brother accused petitioner No. 2 asked the complainant to bring Tic. 1 lac from her father. But her father was unable to pay the amount and petitioner Nos. 1 and 2 out of anger kicked the complainant and kept her confined in a room for 2 days without giving any food. The accused petitioners also tortured her, took her ornaments and drove her out from the house with the threat that if she fails to bring Tk. 1 lac she would not be allowed to come back. Stating those facts she lodged a General Diary on 15.5.98 with the police station. The accused petitioners, however, came to know about lodging of the G. D. and they went to the house of her father and with the assurance that the complaint would live in their house with respect and affection then they took her to their house. But on her return the accused petitioners again started physically torturing her causing injuries and held out threat to kill her. After hearing about this incident her father took her to the hospital where she was given treatment. Thereafter on obtaining a medical certificate she filed the petition of complaint in the Court of Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Chittagong for an offence punishable under Sections 10(2)/14 of the Nari-O-Shishu Nirjatan (Bishesh Bidhan) Ain, 1995. The learned Magistrate sent the petition to the officer in charge, Double Mooring P.S. for investigation. A Sub-Inspector of Police after completion of investigation submitted a charge sheet on 31.7.98 under the aforesaid sections. On receipt of the charge sheet the learned Judge, Nari-O-Shishu Nirjatan (Bishesh) Adalat, Chittagong on 12.10.98 started Nari-O-Shishu Case No. 156 of 1998 and took cognizance of the offence under the aforesaid sections of the Act (Ain). 

 3. During pendency of the case before the learned Judge the accused-petitioners tiled an application under section 498 Cr. P. C. for anticipatory (pre-arrest) bail in the High Court Division and the learned Judges issued a Rule Nisi upon the State-respondent to show cause as to why the accused petitioners should not be granted anticipatory bail and also granted an ad interim bail. But a Division Bench of the High Court Division after hearing discharged the Rule, recalled the order of ad interim bail, and directed the accused petitioners to surrender before the learned Judge. 

 5. The learned Judges of the High Court Division found that there is allegation of assault on the complainant by all the accused petitioners, that the charge sheet was already submitted and that the learned Judge of the Court below took cognizance of the offence. The impugned judgment and order were passed upon such findings. It has been consistently held by this Division that pre-arrest bail should not be granted after submission of charge sheet and/or after cognizance of the offence taken by the trial court unless exceptional circumstances exist calling for exercise of a discretionary power under section 498 Cr. P. C. In the instant case no such circum-stances exist. The impugned judgment and order do not call for any interference.
